punchline: Ferriss's fear exercise adds the column most people forget: what staying put costs.
thirty_sec: Tim Ferriss has a three-step exercise he calls fear-setting. On paper, you write the worst that could happen if you did the scary thing, then what you could do to recover, and then what it costs you to do nothing over one, five and ten years. Most of us only ever write the first part. The third part is the one that makes standing still look like a choice with a price.
